opportunities.goal: Return exact linear-contrast bounds over declared glyph alternatives, shared calibration offsets and sparse row errors, with extremal witnesses.
opportunities.successMetric: Bounds and witnesses agree with an independently authored exhaustive oracle on every valid finite case; unsupported cases are refused. Technical correctness does not pass the separate novelty or market gate.
opportunities.thesis: Test whether an explicitly specified linear contrast can be answered without selecting one transcription, preserving glyph ambiguity, shared calibration and sparse source errors. Established certain-answer and query-cleaning methods challenge novelty; flagship status is withheld.
opportunities.title: Archival claim rescue with preserved uncertainty

sources.excerpt: The paper treats certainty over incomplete data, including bag semantics and value-inventing queries using arithmetic and aggregation. It is direct prior art against a broad claim that query-level certainty is newly invented.
sources.title: Knowledge-Preserving Certain Answers for SQL-like Queries

sources.excerpt: The authors use query information and possible-world semantics to choose which uncertain data to clean under limited resources, with quality measures and efficient algorithms. Query-directed uncertainty reduction is established prior art.
sources.title: Cleaning Uncertain Data with Quality Guarantees

sources.excerpt: Zhang and Sieber describe a modular workflow combining layout processing and handwriting recognition for historical weather records, evaluated with DRAW material. This motivates the problem; it does not validate the present authored glyph or calibration sets. First published 26 September 2024.
sources.title: Automation of historical weather data rescue
